backlogged.summary: approve.mjs's roundsExhausted() decides the 'blocked after max_rounds' refusal purely from verdict count (contractVerdicts(...).length >= maxRounds + extra) without checking the actual block reason stored nowhere on the feature. If a feature is blocked for reason 'needs_human' (or 2 consecutive eval_errors) and that happens to land on/after the round-count threshold, a plain `harness approve F<n>` wrongly reports 'F<n> is blocked after max_rounds with this contract — change the contract, or pass --extra-round...' even though the block had nothing to do with running out of rounds — AC-1's own text scopes the refusal to '(reason rounds)'. Verified with a scripted repro (3 verdicts: fail, fail, needs-human, all sharing one contract hash) where a plain re-approve throws the max_rounds message instead of succeeding. Workaround (--extra-round) still unblocks the feature, and SPEC §7.6 already generalizes the count-based rule to stall/divergence explicitly, so this may be accepted design rather than an oversight for needs_human specifically — flagging for a human decision rather than blocking.

The max-rounds-exceeded check ('k > maxRounds && k >= allowed') is duplicated verbatim in lib/eval-status.mjs (decideStatus) and lib/run.mjs (endRound's `limit()`), and the default max_rounds fallback ('Number.isInteger(config.max_rounds) && config.max_rounds > 0 ? config.max_rounds : 3') is repeated a third time in lib/commands/approve.mjs. A future change to the round-limit rule would need to be kept in sync by hand across three files.
